agent_explanation: Both bodies start at rest (step 0, zero momentum) so any net momentum at step 1 is integration error. At step 1 the impulses m*dv do not cancel: m0*dv ~ 0.526 vs m1*dv ~ 0.585 in different directions, leaving net (mx,my)=(-0.036,0.046). Smaller dt and smaller G still fail, but equal masses pass, pointing to mass-ratio-dependent asymmetry. Likely cause: pairwise forces not applied as equal-and-opposite at the same instant (e.g. per-body adaptive substepping or sequential position updates), so the light body's large acceleration and heavy body's small acceleration are integrated over different effective intervals/positions and Newton's third law is broken discretely.
